"Many amendments are technical or administrative in nature. Some amendments resulted from differing interpretations of the Constitution by the judiciary and Parliament. Many amendments were the result of a consensus among political parties. The 42nd Amendment was passed during the Emergency and was very controversial."
(i) Explain the term 'technical amendments', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The 44th Amendment was passed in 1978. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The 42nd Amendment was passed after wide consultation in normal times." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) Amendments that clarify or change technical details, such as the retirement age of judges. (ii) The new government wanted to undo the changes made during the Emergency by the 42nd Amendment. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was passed during the Emergency and was controversial.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Amendments that clarify or change technical details, such as the retirement age of judges. (ii) The new government wanted to undo the changes made during the Emergency by the 42nd Amendment. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was passed during the Emergency and was controversial.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the basic structure doctrine and the evolution of the Constitution:
I. The Indian Constitution has never changed since 1950.
II. The basic structure doctrine has set limits on Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.
III. Judicial interpretation has expanded the meaning of rights such as the right to life.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (a) I is incorrect: It has evolved through amendments, judgements and practice. II is correct. III is correct.
options: II and III only
I and II only
III only
I only

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about how the Constitution is amended:
I. Some parts of the Constitution can be changed by Parliament through a simple majority.
II. Amendments affecting federal features also require the ratification of half the states.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The basic structure doctrine protects the core of the Constitution.
Reason (R): It prevents a temporary majority in Parliament from destroying democracy, federalism or rights.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: it prevents a temporary majority in Parliament from destroying democracy, federalism or rights.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the basic structure doctrine and the evolution of the Constitution and answer the questions that follow.
"The basic structure doctrine has itself become a part of the Constitution through judicial interpretation. Judicial interpretation has expanded the meaning of rights such as the right to life. The basic structure doctrine has set limits on Parliament's power to amend the Constitution."
(i) The Supreme Court ruled in the Indra Sawhney case of 1992 that reservations should normally not exceed: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'basic structure doctrine' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The basic structure doctrine protects the core of the Constitution. (2)
items.answer: (i) 50 per cent (ii) The principle that Parliament cannot amend the basic features of the Constitution, such as democracy, federalism and judicial review. (iii) It prevents a temporary majority in Parliament from destroying democracy, federalism or rights.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) 50 per cent (ii) The principle that Parliament cannot amend the basic features of the Constitution, such as democracy, federalism and judicial review. (iii) It prevents a temporary majority in Parliament from destroying democracy, federalism or rights.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about how the Constitution is amended is NOT correct?
items.answer: The Indian Constitution can be amended only by a referendum.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. It is amended by Parliament; there is no referendum.
options: There is no provision for a referendum in the amendment procedure in India.
The Indian Constitution can be amended only by a referendum.
Most amendments require a special majority in each House of Parliament.
The Indian Constitution combines rigidity and flexibility in its amendment procedure.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to why the Constitution has been amended so often.
(a) Give a reason for the following: Many amendments did not change the basic philosophy of the Constitution. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "The 44th Amendment extended the term of the Lok Sabha to six years." (2)
items.answer: (a) They were technical or reflected agreement among parties. (b) The 42nd did; the 44th restored the five-year term.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – they were technical or reflected agreement among parties. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – The 42nd did; the 44th restored the five-year term. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: In the study of the basic structure doctrine and the evolution of the Constitution, the term 'living document' refers to:
items.answer: A constitution that evolves through amendments, judicial interpretation and political practice
items.markingKey: (a) 'living document' means a constitution that evolves through amendments, judicial interpretation and political practice.
options: A constitution that evolves through amendments, judicial interpretation and political practice
Amendments that clarify or change technical details, such as the retirement age of judges
The balance in the Indian Constitution between provisions that are hard to change and those that are easy to change
A majority of the total membership of a House and two-thirds of the members present and voting

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the basic structure doctrine and the evolution of the Constitution:
I. The Constitution has survived because it is flexible enough to respond to new situations.
II. The basic structure doctrine has set limits on Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about why the Constitution has been amended so often:
I. Some amendments resulted from differing interpretations of the Constitution by the judiciary and Parliament.
II. The 42nd Amendment was passed after wide consultation in normal times.
III. The 42nd Amendment was passed during the Emergency and was very controversial.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (d) I is correct. II is incorrect: It was passed during the Emergency and was controversial. III is correct.
options: II only
All of them
III only
I and III only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on why the Constitution has been amended so often and answer the questions that follow.
"Some amendments resulted from differing interpretations of the Constitution by the judiciary and Parliament. The 42nd Amendment was passed during the Emergency and was very controversial. Many amendments were the result of a consensus among political parties."
(i) The 42nd Amendment extended the term of the Lok Sabha from five to: (1)
(ii) Explain the term '42nd Amendment' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Constitution has been amended many times. (2)
items.answer: (i) six years (ii) The extensive amendment of 1976, made during the Emergency, which changed many provisions of the Constitution. (iii) Technical changes, differing interpretations and political consensus have all needed amendments.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) six years (ii) The extensive amendment of 1976, made during the Emergency, which changed many provisions of the Constitution. (iii) Technical changes, differing interpretations and political consensus have all needed amendments.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? A majority of the total membership of a House and two-thirds of the members present and voting.
items.answer: special majority
items.markingKey: (b) special majority: a majority of the total membership of a House and two-thirds of the members present and voting.
options: ratification by states
special majority
living document
amendment

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the basic structure doctrine and the evolution of the Constitution is correct?
items.answer: Judicial interpretation has expanded the meaning of rights such as the right to life.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: It was laid down by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case. It prevents Parliament from changing the basic features. It has evolved through amendments, judgements and practice.
options: The Indian Constitution has never changed since 1950.
Judicial interpretation has expanded the meaning of rights such as the right to life.
The basic structure doctrine was laid down by Parliament.
The basic structure doctrine allows Parliament to change any feature of the Constitution.

items.stem:
Statement: The 44th Amendment was passed in 1978.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The new government wanted to undo the changes made during the Emergency by the 42nd Amendment.
items.markingKey: (a) The new government wanted to undo the changes made during the Emergency by the 42nd Amendment.
options: The new government wanted to undo the changes made during the Emergency by the 42nd Amendment.
They were technical or reflected agreement among parties.
It prevents a temporary majority in Parliament from destroying democracy, federalism or rights.
Technical changes, differing interpretations and political consensus have all needed amendments.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to how the Constitution is amended.
(a) Give a reason for the following: The Constitution can respond to new circumstances. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "A deadlock on an amendment bill can be resolved by a joint sitting." (2)
items.answer: (a) Its amendment procedure allows changes when there is wide agreement. (b) Each House must pass it separately; no joint sitting.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – its amendment procedure allows changes when there is wide agreement. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – Each House must pass it separately; no joint sitting. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the basic structure doctrine and the evolution of the Constitution is NOT correct?
items.answer: The basic structure doctrine was laid down by Parliament.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. It was laid down by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case.
options: The basic structure doctrine was laid down by Parliament.
The Indian Constitution has evolved through amendments, court judgements and political practice.
The basic structure doctrine has itself become a part of the Constitution through judicial interpretation.
Judicial interpretation has expanded the meaning of rights such as the right to life.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on how the Constitution is amended and answer the questions that follow.
"An amendment bill must be passed separately by both Houses, with no joint sitting. There is no provision for a referendum in the amendment procedure in India. Most amendments require a special majority in each House of Parliament."
(i) Amendments affecting the distribution of powers between the Union and states also need ratification by: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'special majority' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Constitution is neither too rigid nor too flexible. (2)
items.answer: (i) at least half of the state legislatures (ii) A majority of the total membership of a House and two-thirds of the members present and voting. (iii) Some parts can be changed by simple majority while others need a special majority and ratification by states.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) at least half of the state legislatures (ii) A majority of the total membership of a House and two-thirds of the members present and voting. (iii) Some parts can be changed by simple majority while others need a special majority and ratification by states.

items.stem: Which of these amendments was passed through political consensus?
items.answer: The 61st Amendment reducing the voting age to 18
items.markingKey: (c) The 61st Amendment reducing the voting age to 18.
options: The 38th Amendment
The 39th Amendment
The 61st Amendment reducing the voting age to 18
The 42nd Amendment of 1976
